title: capacity-scenario-lab-weekly-capture-2026-11-20
content:
Weekly capture from the Capacity Scenario Lab (session grouped notes and quick triage). This doc is the working record for the lab runs performed 2026-11-18 through 2026-11-20. Purpose: exercise hedging and prewarm knobs, validate cross-region failover behavior under mixed traffic, and collect telemetry for cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Summary:
- Ran 6 synthetic scenarios across 3 regions (us-west, eu-north, ap-southeast) focused on: sudden regional load spike, region failover (graceful and abrupt), mixed-sequence-length workload, and long-tail cold-start readback.
- Primary goals met: validated automated hedging rule triggers, confirmed prewarm factor improvements reduce 95th percentile token-latency by ~18% for burst traffic, and surfaced a persistent KV-cache miss pattern during multi-model routing.
- Remaining concerns: prewarm cost impact on low-utilization pools, a kernel-selection regression on certain quantized model builds causing 5-7% throughput drop in ap-southeast.

Key metrics observed (session aggregates):
- Peak concurrent inference requests simulated: 25k rps (across regions).
- GPUs online (pool): us-west 480, eu-north 320, ap-southeast 200.
- Average GPU utilization during spikes: us-west 68%, eu-north 72%, ap-southeast 61% (ap region shows higher variance).
- 95th percentile token-latency without prewarm (baseline): 190ms; with prewarm factor=1.8: 155ms.
- KV cache hit-rate during multi-model router test: dropped from 73% to 51% during cross-model spillovers.
- Cost delta (estimated): prewarm factor=1.8 increases short-run GPU-minutes by ~12% but reduces token processing latency-related SLA penalties in simulated customer billing model.

What we ran (brief):
- Lab run lab-2026-11-19-03: abrupt region failover (kill control-plane node in eu-north) while routing policy applied weighted hedging. Observed routing fallback to us-west within 6s; instances in ap-southeast briefly absorbed overflow, causing transient KV-cache thrash.
- Lab run lab-2026-11-19-09: burst traffic with mixed seq lengths (avg 150 tokens, heavy tail to 2048). Evaluated batching windows and kernel selection. ap-southeast run showed kernel fallback to slower execution path for quantized 7B variant (tracked to recent PR).
- Lab run lab-2026-11-20-01: controlled prewarm sweep (factor 1.0 -> 2.2). Measured steady-state cost and tail latency improvements.

Observations and analysis:
- Prewarm benefits: consistent reduction in tail latency for cold-sensitive workflows (chat-style sessions with repeated short prompts). Prewarm factor above 1.5 has diminishing latency returns but linear cost growth. We should define cost/latency operating bands per customer tier.
- KV cache thrash: when multi-model routing spills into regions with different hot-set distributions we see severe cache invalidation. This suggests we should: (a) add routing affinity for model-hot regions, and (b) explore global prefix-aware warmers that can prime new region caches during failover.
- Kernel-selection regression: ap-southeast throughput drop tied to optimizer change in PR #1409 (runtime picks fall-back kernel for specific matmul shapes after quantization pass). Repro steps and mitigations in linked GH PR.
- Autoscaler sensitivity: the current scale-up window (30s) causes missed short bursts. In the lab we tested shortening to 12s and observed more aggressive scaling but higher churn. Trade-off: faster response vs. degraded mean-time-to-recover due to preemption on some clouds.

Decisions made in-session:
- Short-term: enable prewarm_factor=1.6 as default for hedged routes that opt-in (experiment bucket), rollout via feature flag to Dedicated clusters first (INFRA-2319).
- Medium-term: implement region-cache priming prototype (contrib task) to be used during automatic failover; scope: prime most common KVs for top-10 models per customer.
- Investigation: assign owners to root-cause PR for kernel-selection. If reproduction confirmed, roll back optimizer change in the affected model packaging pipeline.

Action items (owners and dates):
- Marta: draft cost-vs-latency banding doc for prewarm profiles and propose default per-customer tier (due 2026-11-26) (Jira: INFRA-2324).
- Ethan: drive kernel regression reproduction and attach perf traces + minimal repro; open hotfix PR if confirmed (due 2026-11-23).
- Li: prototype region-cache priming tool and run it in lab against eu-north->us-west failover (due 2026-12-03).
- Priya: run controlled customer-sim billing model to validate prewarm cost offsets and prepare a one-pager for product (due 2026-11-30).
- Jonas: evaluate autoscaler sensitivity window adjustments across cloud providers and produce a recommendation matrix (due 2026-11-29).

Meeting notes (stand-up style snippet from 2026-11-20 quick sync):
Attendees: Marta, Ethan, Li, Priya, Jonas, Arun (SRE), Kelsey (Product)
- Marta: summary of lab runs, recommended default prewarm factor 1.6 for experiment group.
- Ethan: kernel regression suspected, will confirm.
- Li: cache priming looks promising — initial prototype will use model-topk prefixes.
- Arun: SRE flagged higher churn when autoscaler window shortened; needs canary in staging.
- Kelsey: product wants conservative rollout for Hosted customers; recommended Dedicated first.

Risks and unknowns:
- Prewarm increases committed GPU-minutes and may push cost beyond some customers' budgets if enabled widely. Need telemetry and opt-in gating.
- Global cache priming could leak sensitive prefixes if not carefully scoped — will need review with security/compliance.
- Back-compat: kernel fallback may affect some older quantized model pack manifests; must ensure semver bumping in model catalog.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (work-in-progress):
- Consider a hybrid prewarm policy: maintain a small warm pool always for high-SLA tiers and ephemeral prewarm for burst windows based on traffic prediction. Investigate using short-history forecasting (5–15m) to trigger ephemeral prewarm.
- Could combine per-customer hotset telemetry with routing affinity matrix to reduce cache thrash during failover. Score candidates by cross-region overlap.

Referenced artifacts and quick links:
- INFRA-2319 (prewarm rollout plan): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2319
- Kernel regression PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423
- Capacity Scenario Lab confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/567890123/Capacity+Scenario+Lab

Next lab window planned: 2026-11-27 to test region-cache priming + prewarm-factor 1.6 canary in dedicated west-asia region.

If you want a quick TL;DR to forward to Product: prewarm reduces tail latency meaningfully in bursts but costs rise; we recommend starting Dedicated canary at factor 1.6, prototype region-cache priming to mitigate KV miss spikes, and block rollbacks on the kernel regression until a fix is validated.
